metadata.note: The D&H's Chateaugay and Lake Placid line - 80 miles from Plattsburgh on Lake Champlain across the northern Adirondacks to Lake Placid, and one of the few American narrow-gauge main lines to be rebuilt to standard gauge and kept running. It began as an industrial and penal railway, not a tourist one: in 1878 the State of New York built a 17-mile 3-foot-gauge line from Plattsburgh to Clinton Prison at Dannemora, laid by prison labour, and in 1879 the Chateaugay Iron Company's Chateaugay Railroad carried it on to the iron mines at Lyon Mountain to bring out ore and charcoal - the first Lyon Mountain ore train reached Plattsburgh on December 18, 1879. The Adirondack tourist trade came later, as the Chateaugay Railway pushed west to Standish (1885), Loon Lake (1886) and Saranac Lake village (December 5, 1887). The Delaware & Hudson financed that last push, organised the dual-gauge Saranac & Lake Placid Railroad in 1890 (opened 1893), took control of the system in 1901, and in 1903 combined everything as the Chateaugay & Lake Placid Railway and converted the whole line to standard gauge. At its height it was a genuine resort route - by 1908 sleeping cars ran through from New York to Lake Placid without change, and Saranac Lake's Union Depot handled 18 to 20 scheduled passenger trains a day in its peak years of 1912-1940, shared with the New York Central. Decline was fast: by 1941 the D&H was down to one train a day to Saranac Lake and back, and in 1946 it pulled out of the Adirondacks altogether, selling the 10-mile Saranac Lake-Lake Placid right of way to the New York Central and moving to abandon service west of Lyon Mountain. The Dannemora-Lyon Mountain branch was lifted in 1969 after the Republic Steel mine closed in 1967; Saranac Lake-Lake Placid, under New York Central and successors, was finally abandoned in 1972 and is now the Adirondack Rail Trail. Station order: Plattsburgh - Dannemora - Lyon Mountain - Standish - Loon Lake - Saranac Lake - Ray Brook - Lake Placid.

geometry_sources: Wikimedia Commons map data behind the Delaware and Hudson Railway article's system map (Data:New York and Canada Railroad.map, CC-BY-4.0), which is OSM-derived. The through route is assembled from four of that layer's features, which chain end to end with ZERO gaps - every join measured 0.000 km: 'Plattsburgh and Dannemora Railroad' (four pieces, Plattsburgh-Dannemora), 'Chateaugay Railroad' (Dannemora-Lyon Mountain), 'Chateaugay Railway' (Lyon Mountain-Saranac Lake) and 'Saranac & Lake Placid Rail Road' (Saranac Lake-Lake Placid). Total 128.9 km / 80.1 miles, with no straight-line approximation anywhere.

Independently cross-checked against OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API), where the corridor is tagged as 'Chateaugay Branch' (20 ways), 'Lake Placid Branch' (30 ways) and the 'Adirondack Rail Trail' (57 ways). Agreement is sub-metre at the median for all three features: Plattsburgh-Lyon Mountain 0.6 m (p90 15.5 m), Lyon Mountain-Saranac Lake 3.3 m (p90 26.0 m), Saranac Lake-Lake Placid 0.5 m (p90 1.9 m).

CAVEAT - this is the ORIGINAL narrow-gauge alignment. The 1903 standard-gauge conversion involved real relocations, and the Commons layer carries them as separate features that are NOT drawn here: a 'Plattsburgh and Dannemora Railroad (Standard Gauge Line)' variant, a 'Plattsburgh Bypass, c. 190x', and six 'Chateaugay and Lake Placid Railway (Standard Gauge Alignment)' segments, the largest of which is a 16.1 km reroute between roughly 44.7460,-73.8517 and 44.6836,-73.9917 in the Dannemora-Lyon Mountain section. So for the post-1903 segments below the dates are right but the geometry is the pre-conversion route.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact timetables; every frequency below is estimated and unsourced, apart from the sourced qualitative anchors (18-20 trains a day at Saranac Lake Union Depot 1912-1940, one train daily by 1941). The START of PASSENGER service is not directly sourced for any section - the line was built for iron ore, charcoal and prison labour, and passenger service is described only as having been added as Adirondack tourist interest grew; the opening years used below are the dates the TRACK reached each point. The END dates are likewise imprecise: 1946 is used throughout because that is the well-sourced year the D&H pulled out of the Adirondacks, but one source says D&H passenger service in the area ended 'in the 1960s', which may mean a residual local service on the Plattsburgh-Lyon Mountain section outlasted the through trains. Note also that the Saranac Lake-Lake Placid section did keep passenger service after 1946 under NEW YORK CENTRAL ownership until the mid-1960s - that is a different railroad and is not represented by this file. The 1932 Winter Olympics specials to Lake Placid are documented as New York Central Adirondack Division trains from Utica and New York, NOT as D&H trains, so no Olympic traffic is claimed here.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
